channels.name: Discover, Grow, Bloom with Garden Marcus
channels.why: Calm, warm garden lessons with songs and movement invite little ones to touch soil, plant seeds, and wonder how living things grow.
channels.note: Kids' spin-off of Garden Marcus (Marcus Bridgewater); low-stimulation, wholesome, aimed at toddlers/preschool; short-to-medium episodes.

channels.name: KidsGardening.org
channels.why: A nonprofit that turns real garden projects into hands-on discovery, showing kids how to sprout seeds, build planters, and observe plant life cycles.
channels.note: Educator/parent-facing how-to and activity videos; steady library, family- and classroom-friendly.

channels.name: Children's Gardening Coach (Skinny Jean Gardener)
channels.why: UK children's gardening coach (Blue Peter's) makes growing feel like a playful adventure with school-garden tours and easy grow-along projects for kids.
channels.note: Lee Connelly; recently rebranded from Skinny Jean Gardener; energetic but advertiser-safe, kid-focused.

channels.name: Guiding Green Thumbs
channels.why: Gentle, clear how-to videos on planting, saving seeds, and welcoming bees and butterflies spark the urge to start a real backyard garden.
channels.note: Zone-5 organic kitchen and flower gardening; calm long-form; adult host but easy for older kids to follow.

channels.name: Huw Richards
channels.why: A grower who started his own channel at age 12 shows how to raise loads of food from almost nothing, proving kids can grow real harvests.
channels.note: Permaculture / grow-your-own; long-form; some episodes are advanced but inspiring for tweens.

channels.name: GrowVeg
channels.why: Friendly animated diagrams and garden walkthroughs explain the why behind planting, crop rotation, and composting so growing makes sense.
channels.note: Ben Vanheems; polished, no-nonsense vegetable-gardening guides; long-form, very advertiser-safe.

channels.name: Boxlapse
channels.why: Mesmerizing seed-to-fruit time-lapses let kids watch weeks of hidden root and shoot growth unfold in minutes, sparking pure botanical wonder.
channels.note: Finland-based; mostly music/no narration; compilation videos run several minutes; universally kid-safe.

channels.name: Neil Bromhall
channels.why: Beautiful studio time-lapses of germinating seeds and opening flowers reveal the secret motion of plants that kids never get to see in real time.
channels.note: Professional plant/flower/fungi time-lapses; short-to-medium, calm; best-guess handle (channel also at youtube.com/user/neilbromhall).

channels.name: MIgardener
channels.why: Started at 16, Luke shows how a few cheap seeds become a whole garden, teaching frugal, organic growing that empowers kids to start their own plot.
channels.note: Organic grow-from-seed and homesteading; frequent long-form uploads; adult host, great for motivated tweens.

channels.name: Carnivorous Plants Hub
channels.why: Care guides and close-ups of Venus flytraps and pitcher plants tap into kids' fascination with plants that catch and eat insects.
channels.note: Enthusiast-run carnivorous-plant growing; how-to and update videos; mild bug-eating footage, fine for curious 8-12s.

channels.name: Epic Gardening
channels.why: In-depth, well-shot grow guides answer endless how-and-why plant questions, making it the go-to hub for kids ready to garden seriously.
channels.note: Large channel central to the niche (Kevin Espiritu); long-form, advertiser-safe; adult-oriented but broadly kid-appropriate.
